label: Claude Code
prompt:
Make a TypeScript program for a shopping cart. The program adds an item to the shopping cart. The program shows the items in the shopping cart. The program removes an item from the shopping cart.

use a functional style.

Write every file in the current directory. Do not use sudo and do not change anything outside this directory.
The code must typecheck with TypeScript 7.0.2, strict, target ES2022, module ESNext, and moduleResolution bundler.
Write .ts files only. Do not write JSX. Do not import a package or a Node built-in module.
A relative import does not need a file extension.
Put an export in every .ts file so TypeScript treats the file as a module.
final_text:
I'm done with the typecheck. It reported no errors, so the program is finished.

The program is three files in the current directory:

- **`cart.ts`** has the cart logic as pure functions on an immutable `Cart`, a read-only array of items. `addItem` returns a new cart. If an item with the same id is already there, it adds the quantities together. `removeItem` returns a new cart without the item that has the given id. An unknown id leaves the cart unchanged. `showCart` returns the cart as text: numbered lines for each item, then the total, or "The shopping cart is empty." Prices are whole cents to avoid floating-point errors.
- **`main.ts`** is a demo. It adds three items, adds more of one of them, shows the cart, removes one item and shows the cart again.
- **`tsconfig.json`** sets strict, ES2022, ESNext modules and bundler resolution, with `noEmit`.

I ran TypeScript 7.0.2 on the project with `tsc -p . --noEmit`, using a copy already cached in `~/.npm/_npx`, so nothing was installed. I did not run the program. Node can't run `main.ts` directly because of the extensionless `./cart` import.

`main.ts` declares its own minimal `console` type, so it doesn't depend on DOM or Node type definitions.
